solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: See poet in my Italian region

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see, as in 'lo and behold'

indicators.note: the poet is placed in the middle of the letters of 'my'

parts.note: taken as written
a bard is a poet

explanation.surface: An invitation to visit the region of Italy where a poet of yours lives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a command to look at the region, but it is the old exclamation lo, and 'in' places the poet within 'my'.
explanation.definitionFit: Lombardy is the northern Italian province around Milan, so it is an example of a region of that country.

clue.text: Rules in Wales somehow putting English off

indicators.note: somehow suggests the letters of Wales are arranged in some other way
putting English off means its abbreviation is removed from the letters of Wales before rearranging

explanation.surface: A remark that Welsh regulations somehow sideline the English.
explanation.walkthrough: Take E out of WALES, leaving WALS, then rearrange those letters as the anagram signal says.
explanation.definitionFit: Laws are the regulations a society lives by, so they are its rules.

clue.text: Disclosure of fellow with uncertainty, beginning to embarrass Victoria maybe

parts.note: a man is a fellow
an if is a doubt or uncertainty, as in 'no ifs or buts'

indicators.note: the beginning of the word embarrass is its first letter

parts.note: Victoria is a London railway station, so it is an example of a station

explanation.surface: A man's doubtful revelation that is set to embarrass Queen Victoria.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Victoria' looks like the queen, but here it is Victoria, a major railway station in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifestation is an outward showing or revealing of something, close to a disclosure.

clue.text: Having muscles pulling creates a state of preoccupation

parts.note: abs is short for abdominal muscles
traction is the action of pulling, as on a limb in hospital

explanation.surface: Someone working the stomach muscles finds their mind drifting.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstraction is absent-mindedness, a state of being lost in thought and preoccupied.

clue.text: In valley wife and daughter take their time

indicators.note: the wife and daughter letters are placed in the middle of the valley word

parts.note: a dale is a valley, especially in northern England

explanation.surface: A mother and daughter stroll unhurriedly through a valley.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle is to move slowly and idle along, so dawdlers take their time.

clue.text: Try to get very warm after beginning to shiver

indicators.note: the warm word is placed after the shiver letter
the beginning of the word shiver is its first letter

parts.note: hot means very warm

explanation.surface: Advice to warm up properly once the shivering starts.
explanation.definitionFit: A shot is an attempt, as in 'have a shot at it', so it means a try.

clue.text: Trivial host — he upset nurse coming to house?

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of these words are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A host is upset by a nurse turning up at the door over something trivial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' rearranges TRIVIAL HOST HE. A health visitor is a British community nurse who visits families, especially new mothers, at home.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a health visitor is a community nurse who calls at people's homes, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Suppose the old revolt?

parts.note: a rising is a revolt, and to rise is to revolt

explanation.surface: A question whether the old folk should be imagined rising up.
explanation.definitionFit: To theorise is to speculate or form a hypothesis, so it means to suppose.

clue.text: Achieves victory, having imbibed last of the drinks

indicators.note: imbibed means drunk in, so the victory word takes a letter inside it

parts.note: wins means achieves victory

indicators.note: the last of the word 'the' is its final letter

explanation.surface: A winner who has been drinking celebrates the victory.
explanation.definitionFit: Wines are alcoholic drinks made from grapes, so they are examples of drinks.

clue.text: Sent back uncooked food, creating conflict

indicators.note: sent back means the word for uncooked is read backwards

parts.note: raw means uncooked
fare is food, as in 'simple fare'

explanation.surface: A diner returns raw food to the kitchen and starts a row.
explanation.definitionFit: Warfare is armed fighting between nations, a form of conflict.

clue.text: Uncontrollable rage over the gang getting back together again

indicators.note: uncontrollable means running wild, so the letters of rage are mixed up

parts.note: a ring is a gang of criminals, as in a drugs ring

explanation.surface: A gang reunites in an uncontrollable rage.
explanation.definitionFit: Regathering means assembling once more, so it is coming back together again.

clue.text: Heftier girl newly engaged, one set aflame?

indicators.note: newly suggests the letters are made anew, rearranged into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A bulky girl who has just got engaged is fired up with passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'newly engaged' rearranges HEFTIER GIRL. 'engaged' looks like a romance, but it just extends the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A firelighter is a block of flammable material that is lit to start a fire, so it is set aflame.

clue.text: Copper probing motives for political meetings

indicators.note: probing means getting inside, so the copper letters go into the motives word

parts.note: causes are reasons or motives
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A police officer investigates why political meetings take place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'probing' signals insertion. 'Copper' looks like a police officer, but it is the metal, symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: A caucus is a meeting of party members to choose candidates or policy, so the plural means political meetings.

clue.text: When to drink litres, going to brilliant wine-growing region

indicators.note: drink means take in, so the litres letter goes inside the when word

parts.note: as means when, as in 'as I left'
ace means brilliant or excellent

explanation.surface: A wine buff decides when to drink litres in a brilliant wine region.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to drink' puts L inside AS, giving ALS.
explanation.definitionFit: Alsace, in eastern France, is famous for its white wines, so it is a wine-producing region.

clue.text: Seaside town submerged in festive season

indicators.note: submerged means sunk below the surface, so the answer lies inside these words

explanation.surface: A coastal resort flooded during the Christmas holidays.
explanation.walkthrough: ST IVES is a seaside resort in Cornwall, south-west England.
explanation.definitionFit: St Ives is a Cornish harbour resort, so it is an example of a seaside town.

clue.text: Chemical left at the bottom of store exploding

indicators.note: in a down clue the bottom is the end, so the left letter is placed after the rest
exploding blows apart the letters of store so they land in another order

explanation.surface: A chemical abandoned at the bottom of a shop's storeroom blows up.
explanation.definitionFit: A sterol is an organic compound such as cholesterol, so it is a chemical.

clue.text: Drivers in a breach of public order with applause all round

indicators.note: the applause word goes all round the breach word, holding it inside

parts.note: cheers are shouts of applause
a riot is a violent disturbance, a breach of public order

explanation.surface: Motorists caught up in a disturbance while crowds cheer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drivers' suggests motorists, but these drive horses; 'all round' wraps the applause around the breach.
explanation.definitionFit: Charioteers drive chariots, as in Roman races, so they are drivers.

clue.text: This should not be in wardrobe — mum has no hesitation

definitions.text: This should not be in wardrobe

indicators.note: has no means lacks, so the hesitation letters are taken away from the mum word

parts.note: mother is a fuller word for mum
er is the sound of hesitation in speech

explanation.surface: A mother confidently insists something has no place in the wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Clothes moths lay eggs whose larvae eat wool, so this insect is unwelcome among stored clothes.

clue.text: One goes round back of shop, getting grabbed by wicked person

indicators.note: the shop letter is grabbed, held inside the wicked person word

parts.note: a sinner is a wicked person

indicators.note: the back of the word shop is its last letter

explanation.surface: Someone loitering behind a shop is seized by a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting grabbed by' puts P inside SINNER.
explanation.definitionFit: A spinner is anything that rotates, such as a top or a spinning ball, so it is one that goes round.

clue.text: Enthusiastic about grabbing composer's final piece of music

indicators.note: grabbing means holding, so the enthusiasm word holds the composer letter inside

parts.note: into means keen on, as in 'really into jazz'

indicators.note: the final letter of the word composer's is taken

explanation.surface: A fan seizes upon a composer's last work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grabbing' puts R inside INTO. 'final piece of music' reads as one phrase, but 'final' belongs to the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: An intro is the opening passage of a song, so it is a short piece of music.

clue.text: Carol is smart, wasting little time

indicators.note: wasting means losing, so the time letter is dropped from the smart word

parts.note: to smart is to sting with pain
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A woman named Carol is clever but squanders a moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Carol' looks like a woman's name, but it is the verb meaning sing joyfully.
explanation.definitionFit: To carol is to sing joyfully, especially Christmas songs, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Sort of ruler in gaol, rich, corrupt

indicators.note: corrupt means spoilt or perverted, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A wealthy, crooked ruler ends up behind bars.
explanation.walkthrough: 'corrupt' rearranges GAOL RICH. Gaol is the British spelling of jail.
explanation.definitionFit: An oligarch is one of a small group holding power, often a rich tycoon, so it is a kind of ruler.
